title: autotune: sensible batching/caching defaults + quantization profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Aisha Patel
description: Context: We want safer, opinionated defaults and an autotune path that reduces per-token unit economics for common workloads without surprising latency regressions. This PR bundles three coordinated changes: (1) conservative batching and prefix/KV caching defaults that reduce cost for bursty short-context traffic, (2) model quantization profiles (recommended 4-bit/8-bit configurations) with validation harnesses, and (3) console/CLI unit-economics tooling that surfaces expected token cost and latency impact for a given policy. Motivation: customers repeatedly pick batching/cache settings that either underutilize GPUs or blast latency; manual quant profiles are error-prone. This automates recommendations and provides measurable cost wins. What changed (high level): added an autotune engine service that consumes recent request histograms and suggests per-route defaults; introduced stable quantization profiles and a validation harness for accuracy/regression checks; added a Unit Econ tab in Redwood Console plus a CLI command `rw autotune run` to preview savings. Performance summary: experiments on internal canary workloads show median cost reduction of ~18% and 95th latency increase <= 6ms for typical web-chat traffic. Checklist: - [x] server: autotune engine + scoring pipeline - [x] runtime: apply default batching/caching policies at route creation - [x] quant: new profiles + validation harness + model metadata - [x] console: UI surfaces and API endpoints - [x] cli: preview + export recommendations - [x] metrics: added telemetry for decisioning audit - [x] docs: user guide and API reference - [x] tests: unit, integration, perf harness Notes: this is conservative by design — autotune suggestions are opt-in for existing customers; new routes get the defaults automatically. Linear: ENG-4821 tracks autotune infra; ENG-4872 tracks console work. Related: PRs 41258 and 41321 contain prior autotune prototypes and cost-analysis scripts.

review_comments: Marco Li: Can we make the initial defaults opt-in for existing routes? Risk is changing behavior mid-flight for enterprise customers.
Aisha Patel: Answered: defaults are opt-out for existing routes; only new routes receive defaults. Added explicit migration guide and a feature flag for org admins.
Priya Sharma: Perf results look good but we need a guardrail for very long-context workloads where batching heuristics can increase memory pressure.
Aisha Patel: Added heuristics that lower batch window for requests with >2048 tokens and a safety cap on KV cache population. Updated tests to cover this.
Evan Brooks: Minor: add telemetry tag to identify autotune-suggested vs manual settings in cost dashboards.
Aisha Patel: Added `autotune_source` tag to emitted metrics and updated console to filter by source. Marking as resolved.
Marco Li: Approving after addressing opt-out and long-context guardrails.

release_notes: - Introduces an autotune engine that recommends batching/caching defaults based on request histograms; new routes receive conservative defaults. - Adds stable quantization profiles and a validation harness to recommend safe 4-bit/8-bit configs. - Adds Unit Economics tooling in Console and CLI to preview expected cost and latency impact. - Opt-out migration path and feature flag included. Expected median unit-cost reduction ~18% in canary tests; see docs/autotune.md for rollout and tuning guidance.
